title: Protocol to track the biosynthesis of cholesterol in cultured HCC cells using 13C compound-specific stable isotopic tracers
protocol: Add 4 mL 0.01% BHT solution to all samples in the 15 mL tube.
Tear the sample using the Tissue-Tearor.
Place 15 mL tube with sample and BHT reagent in a larger tube filled with ice.
Insert the Tearor probe into the liquid in the 15 mL tube until the metal reaches near the bottom.
Slowly turn on the Tissue-Tearor to reach 6000–8000 RPM.
Tear the sample for 2 × 20 s pulses, pausing for 10 s between each pulse.
Rinse the Tissue-Tearor in three separate beakers filled with RO water, EtOH, and RO water.
Clean the probe between each sample using RO water.
Replace the first RO water rinse after every new sample.
Pour 5 mL of cold Folch solution into the 15 mL tube containing the sample and BHT solution.
Prepare another clean 15 mL tube with 5 mL of Folch solution for lipid recovery.
Place the 15 mL tube with the sample and BHT reagent in a larger ice-filled tube.
Insert the Tearor probe into the sample tube until near the bottom.
Slowly turn on the Tissue-Tearor to reach speeds between 6000-8000 RPM (6-8 on the motor).
Tear the sample for two pulses of 20 seconds each, pausing in between to cool the sample.
Set aside the processed sample tube on ice.
Slowly turn on the Tissue-Tearor until the speed of 6000–8000 RPM (6–8 on the motor) is reached.
Tear the liquid for 1 × 20 s to remove and collect any sample or lipid adhered to the Tissue-Tearor.
Combine both tubes into one, containing the sample, 4 mL of BHT solution, and 10 mL of Folch.
Rinse the Tissue-Tearor.
Pulse the probe for 20 s in each of three beakers filled with RO water, methanol, and RO water to clean the probe between samples.
Replace the first RO water rinse after every new sample; replace methanol and second RO wash when dirty.
Repeat steps from tearing liquid to rinsing and cleaning probes for all samples.
Store prepared samples, capped, on ice while preparing remaining samples.
Vortex all samples for 30 s.
Flush each tube with N2 gas to prevent lipid oxidation during extraction.
Store samples diagonally on ice.
Place samples on a shaker table for 30 min at 100–150 rpm.
Vortex all samples for 30 s.
Centrifuge all samples for 10 min at 3000 × g.
Separate the sample into two phases.
Collect the lower organic phase with lipids.
Using a pre-combusted glass Pasteur pipette, slowly lower the tip down the side of the tube and into the lower phase.
Push the pipette through any white precipitate layer between the two phases.
Slowly draw up the solution until the pipette is full.
Quickly remove the pipette without drawing in any upper phase and transfer the liquid into a pre-combusted borosilicate culture tube.
Cap the culture tube with plastic caps that have PTFE liners.
Repeat for all samples to collect the entire lower phase.
Dry down the lower phase in culture tubes under a constant stream of N2 gas at approximately 20°C–22°C, avoiding lipid oxidation.
Store the completely dry sample in a −20°C freezer.
Seal the vials with N2 gas during step 9 to prevent lipid oxidation during extraction.
Do not cross-contaminate 12C and 13C treatments.
Use new reagents for rinsing and new lab materials for each treatment group.
Thoroughly clean the Tissue Tearor between processing of each group.
Add 1.5 mL of 0.5 M metholated KOH and 1.5 mL of MQ Water (1:1 ratio) to the culture tubes.
Flush tube with N2 gas and vortex for 30 seconds.
Allow the sample to saponify for 2 hours at approximately 20°C–22°C in the capped glass culture tube.
Place samples on a shaker table at 70 rpm for this duration.
Add 2 mL of hexane-diethyl ether (9:1) solution to the glass culture tube.
Vortex for 30 seconds and allow to settle.
Collect the upper phase containing sterols and fatty acids (neutral lipids).
Using a pre-combusted glass Pasteur pipette, slowly draw-up the upper phase until the pipette is full.
Transfer the liquid into a new pre-combusted borosilicate culture tube.
Cap the tube with plastic caps featuring PTFE liners.
Repeat this process until all of the upper phase is collected.
Extract each sample using hexane-diethyl ether (9:1) solution two additional times, resulting in three total extractions per sample.
Store prepared samples on ice while preparing remaining samples.
Dry down each sample at 50°C under a constant stream of N2 gas until completely dry.
Resolubilize the dried lipid extract in 100 μL aliquots of isooctane and transfer to a clean borosilicate 4 mL vial.
Repeat resolubilization twice, resulting in a total of 200 μL liquid sample in the 4 mL vial.
After each injection of 100 μL isooctane aliquots, briefly roll the solvent around the glass to ensure lipids dissolve completely.
Pipette 100 μL of cholesterol standard (dissolved in EtOH or DCM) into a separate clean glass GC vial.
Dry down each sample under a constant stream of N₂ gas at 50°C until completely dry.
Dissolve lipids in 50 μL of DCM.
Add 100 μL of BSTFA.
Flush vials with N₂ gas.
Shake gently and heat for 30 min at 60°C.
Cool the vials in a fridge for 5 min.
Dry down each sample under a constant stream of N₂ gas until completely dry.
Rinse samples by adding 50 μL of DCM, then drying down under a constant stream of N₂ gas until completely dry.
Add 500 μL DCM and shake gently.
Transfer to a clean GC vial using a pipette.
Repeat the rinse step two more times, resulting in 1.5 mL of DCM and sample in the GC vial.
Analyze samples immediately on GC-C-MS-IRMS for best results.
Analyze 1–2 blanks before analysis, injecting DCM or Ethyl-Acetate.
Analyze the cholesterol standard in duplicate at the beginning.
Analyze each unknown sample at least in duplicate, although triplicate is best to constrain variation.
